# Geometric-mean affine buffers: attainment and a penalty that preserves properness

This is a new extremal interface, not an OC proof. It distinguishes a
proved positive-parameter minimum from the extra proper-own-trace
condition needed for the critical-menu calculus. The latter does NOT
follow automatically from fixed-epsilon compactness.

## 1. Original bad sublevel and the aligned affine parameter

Use a cardinality-minimal original bad canonical base P and the precise
hypotheses of `candidate f7c05b2c30c8cfcb`.
Let d>=1, N=d+1, m=|P|, k=k(P), tau=gamma_d/k, and choose b<tau above
an original bad reference value. After actual continuous GL maps and
affine continuous shears, the entire original sublevel beta_0<=b has
representatives in one compact family A with

    M=1,  V_z>=v>0,  K_z subset R Ball.

All its positive Hausdorff limits satisfy the proper-closed-minor bounds

    V(T)<=b k(T)/gamma_d<k(T)/k.                         (1)

Indeed restriction to T, followed by its canonical lift, has original
normalized depth at least gamma_d/k(T), by the original minimal choice.
The full original depth is at least V(T) times that depth. This proves
(1), not just a counting quota postulated about a prospective minimum.

For every positive affine function ell on B=conv(P), use the aligned
buffer

    f_ell(z,x)=(ell(z) E_(K_z)(x)/M)^(1/N)

and the within-fiber covariance norm G_K(u). Joint concavity, exact
continuous gradient grad_x f_ell=f_ell a_opt, covariance under the actual
normalization maps, and the scoped contact continuation are proved in
`candidate 3101206ec4580190`.
Write beta_epsilon(K,ell) for its normalized maximum actual depth.

Normalize ell by its V-weighted GEOMETRIC mean:

    sum_z w_z log ell(z)=0,       w_z=V_z/M.             (2)

This condition is invariant under common continuous affine coordinate
changes. It fixes the otherwise arbitrary positive scale of ell. In
rank zero it simply gives ell=1.

## 2. Escape of a positive affine parameter exposes one base face

Suppose K_j lies in A, K_j->K, and ell_j satisfies (2). Set

    P_j=sum_z w_jz ell_j(z),    h_j=ell_j/P_j.

Then h_j is positive affine and has weighted arithmetic mean one. Since
all w_jz>=v, its values satisfy 0<h_j(z)<=1/v. In a fixed finite affine
basis this bounds its coefficients. Pass to a subsequence with h_j->h,
where h is nonnegative affine and sum_z w_z h(z)=1.

If h is positive at every sampled base, then its geometric mean converges
to a positive number and

    ell_j=h_j / prod_z h_j(z)^(w_jz)

converges to a positive finite normalized affine function. Otherwise

    F={z in B:h(z)=0}

is a nonempty proper face of B. The denominator in the preceding display
tends to zero: at least one logarithm tends to minus infinity with its
weight bounded below by v, while every other logarithm is bounded above.
Thus

    ell_j(p)->infinity for EVERY sampled p outside F.            (3)

This describes every failure of compactness of the positive geometric-
normalized parameter. No lattice points move in this argument.

## 3. A sufficiently large buffer recovers actual BASE depth

Let all actual fibers lie in R Ball, take y in K_p, and define

    sigma_K=min_(||u||=1) G_K(u)>0.

If

    epsilon f_ell(p,y) sigma_K >=2R,                            (4)

then the buffered depth at (p,y) is exactly its closed pure-base depth.
For every Euclidean unit continuous u and every base tilt a, every fiber
with a.(z-p)>=0 is wholly contained in the buffered cap, since
u.(X-y)>=-2R and the buffer displacement is at least 2R. If a is zero,
all fibers are captured. Otherwise these wholly captured fibers form a
closed pure-base halfspace through p. Every nonvertical buffered cap
therefore has mass at least the minimum pure-base mass at p. The pure-
base family itself is included in the depth infimum, giving equality.

At the ordinary centroid g_p, E_(K_p)(g_p)=V_p. On compact A, V_p>=v
and sigma_K is uniformly positive by covariance continuity. For a FIXED
epsilon>0, (3) therefore implies (4) eventually at every p outside F.

## 4. Unpenalized positive-parameter bad minima are attained

The new finite arithmetic theorem
`candidate 9ae432ab1b731d70`
has independent root and Two-sided audits. It says that under the
NONSTRICT proper-minor quotas V(T)<=k(T)M/k, every proper base face has
an outside point of weighted closed BASE depth at least M/k. It uses
only maximal thresholds and parity; no fiber-volume concavity is assumed.

Fix epsilon>0 and suppose beta_epsilon(K,ell)<=b for a sequence of
normalized pairs. Original depth is at most this value, so the bodies
compactify in A. If ell escaped, Section 2 gives a zero face F. Apply the
arithmetic theorem to the limiting positive weights using (1). Choose
p outside F with limiting base depth at least 1/k. Base depths are
continuous in the finitely many weights. Sections 2--3 then give

    liminf beta_epsilon(K_j,ell_j)>=1/k>b,

a contradiction. Hence the ell parameters also have a positive finite
subsequence limit. Cap-depth continuity follows from the same uniform
slab comparison as before, now including uniform ell convergence.
Therefore the full bad sublevel of PAIRS is compact modulo the permitted
affine maps, for this fixed epsilon.

Consequently, whenever a reference pair has value below b, the infimum
of beta_epsilon over ALL positive compatible families and ALL positive
affine ell satisfying (2) is attained with every fiber and every ell value
positive. This is a genuine joint unrestricted minimum. For all sufficiently
small epsilon the reference ell=1 supplies such a pair.

Let beta_0^* be the original fixed-base infimum, attained in A. Testing
its minimizer with ell=1 and using the uniform slab constant L gives

    beta_0^* <= inf_(K,ell) beta_epsilon(K,ell)
                <= beta_0^*+epsilon L R.                       (5)

Thus these minimum VALUES converge to the original minimum. This does
not assert that every buffered maximizing mark converges to an original
maximizer when ell itself depends on epsilon.

## 5. The remaining properness distinction is real

The parameter compactness in Section 4 is for each FIXED epsilon. It does
not bound ell uniformly as epsilon tends to zero. In particular epsilon
ell^(1/N) need not tend to zero. Thus the earlier small-buffer own-trace
argument cannot be imported into these joint minima without another proof.

Exact safe interval calibrations show both epsilon-dependent optimized
parameter growth and arbitrarily small-epsilon positive normalized parameters
with all-own-full cap plateaus. Those examples are not joint bad minima,
but they refute an unqualified inference from normalization or positivity.

The generalized contact theorem applies whenever its required active own
traces and finite-menu conditions are proved. Positive ell attainment alone
is not that proof. A pure-base-binding or partially saturated stratum must
be treated explicitly, or a different extremal objective must enforce the
properness needed below.

## 6. A penalized objective enforces uniform small physical buffering

There is a fully rigorous alternative that restores uniform properness.
Let

    P(K,ell)=sum_z w_z ell(z)>=1

by weighted AM--GM under (2), and minimize

    J_epsilon(K,ell)=beta_epsilon(K,ell)
                          +epsilon^2 [P(K,ell)-1].               (6)

This objective is invariant under the same actual affine maps. It is at
least beta_0^*. Testing the original minimizer with ell=1 gives

    inf J_epsilon<=beta_0^*+epsilon L R.                         (7)

For sufficiently small epsilon this is below b. A minimizing sequence
therefore has original depth below b, and its bodies lie in A. For fixed
epsilon the nonnegative penalty bounds P and hence every ell(z). Condition
(2), with weights at least v, also bounds every ell(z) away from zero: if
max ell<=A_0, then

    ell(z)>=A_0^(-(1-w_z)/w_z).

Thus the positive parameter domain is compact on this sublevel even
without the face-escape argument. Continuity proves attainment.

More importantly, at an attained minimizing pair (7) and beta_epsilon>=
beta_0^* give

    P<=1+(L R)/epsilon.                                        (8)

Since E_z(x)<=V_z and ell(z)V_z/M<=P, all physical unit-continuous-normal
buffer displacements are bounded uniformly by

    Delta_epsilon=epsilon R[1+(L R)/epsilon]^(1/N) ->0.          (9)

For every candidate, 0<=b_epsilon-b_0<=L Delta_epsilon in the M=1 frame.
The raw maximum is at least c=gamma_d/m, from a largest-fiber centroid.
An actual buffered maximizing mark therefore has original depth at least
c-L Delta_epsilon. Original depth is L-Lipschitz in its fiber and zero
on its boundary. Consequently its distance from that boundary is at least
(c-L Delta_epsilon)/L. Once L Delta_epsilon<c/4, every maximizing mark
has interior distance at least 3c/(4L), while every own buffered shift
is at most Delta_epsilon<c/(4L). ALL its own traces are proper.

This restores the entire proved critical-menu, fixed-face and exact contact
continuation framework at these penalized joint minima, with no assumption
about individual cap regularity: supporting OTHER-fiber traces are handled
by the proved scalar directional inverses. It does not remove the penalty
from a shape variation. Its derivative must be included, as follows.

## 7. Exact normalization and penalty derivatives

For an actual signed radial shape path write

    V_z'=-D_z,    M'=-D,    D=sum_z D_z.

First keep the affine SHAPE of ell fixed and multiply it by the unique
scalar that preserves (2) for the changing weights. At the original
normalized pair, its logarithmic derivative is

    s=ell_z'/ell_z=(1/M)sum_z D_z log ell_z,                     (10)

independent of z. To check (10), differentiate sum w_z log ell_z=0,
use w_z'=(w_z D-D_z)/M, and use the old zero logarithmic mean.

The aligned buffer has exact fixed-mark derivative

    f_z'/f_z=(1/N)[-C_z/E_z+D/M+s],                              (11)

where C_z is the actual own projective-kernel boundary loss. The contact
minimum retains this term at EVERY old marked contact; its values f_z
on a homothetic face need not be equal.

The penalty's arithmetic factor obeys

    P'=(1/M)sum_z D_z [P(1+log ell_z)-ell_z].                    (12)

This follows by differentiating sum w_z ell_z and substituting (10).
There is no asserted sign for (12).

For a fixed body and an arbitrary affine perturbation phi, normalize
ell+t phi geometrically. Then

    ell_z'=phi(z)-ell_z A_phi,
    A_phi=sum_z w_z phi(z)/ell_z,
    P'=sum_z w_z phi(z)-P A_phi.                                 (13)

Under regular singleton critical groups, set delta_i=epsilon f_i/B_i.
Their exact raw covering derivative is

    q_i'=(delta_i/N)[phi(p_i)/ell_i-A_phi].                      (14)

Thus an interior minimum of the UNPENALIZED objective requires some
eta_i>=0, sum eta=1, satisfying, for every affine phi,

    sum_i eta_i delta_i phi(p_i)/ell_i
       =(sum_i eta_i delta_i) sum_z w_z phi(z)/ell_z.            (15)

The tilted base barycenter with weights w_z/ell_z therefore lies in the
convex hull of the active witness bases. This is a necessary condition
from nonexistence of a simultaneous strict decrease of the actual cover,
not a presumed derivative of the global maximum.

For the penalized objective (6), the exact condition instead is

 sum_i eta_i delta_i phi(p_i)/ell_i + N M epsilon^2 sum_z w_z phi(z)
   = [sum_i eta_i delta_i+N M epsilon^2 P]
                          sum_z w_z phi(z)/ell_z.               (16)

This follows by applying the same finite separation to
q_i'/M+epsilon^2 P' and multiplying by NM. All coefficients on either
side of (16) are nonnegative, but no ratio is assumed uniformly small.
In particular a small absolute penalty does not automatically make its
stationarity term negligible relative to every source credit.

For nonregular groups, or multiple contacts, use their exact contact
minimum and scalar inverse responses before asserting a linear identity.
Equations (15)--(16) are explicitly regular-singleton statements.

## 8. Precise present scope

The affine weighting and the new face quota lemma produce an attained
positive unpenalized parameter minimum. A separate penalized objective
produces an attained minimum with uniformly proper own shifted sections,
and its values still tend exactly to the original fixed-base infimum.
All normalization/penalty derivatives are explicit.

Neither result proves that the simultaneous physical covering response
pays gamma_d/k. That numerical or structural theorem is still missing.
These constructions are new admissible extremal settings, not a substitute
for that proof and not a claim that OC has been resolved.
